newsitem.title: USA: D.R. Horton sees lower SG&A costs in future.
newsitem.headline: D.R. Horton sees lower SG&A costs in future.

text.p: D.R. Horton Inc said Tuesday that it expects its selling, general and administrative expenses to decline over the remainder of the year as recent acquisitions come on line. The company said that record March home sales and quarter-end sales backlog will provide continued momentum as it enters the peak selling season.

As previously released, new sales orders for the quarter ended March 31 increased 25 percent to 1,281 homes ($212.4 million), from 1,028 homes ($174.9 million) for the same period of 1996, while backlog at March 31, increased 42 percent to 1,841 homes ($324.5 million), the highest in the history of the company, said Horton.
New sales orders for the first six months of fiscal 1997 increased to 2,032 homes ($342.1 million) from 1,727 homes ($290.3 million) for the same period of 1996.
